turns.content: I’ve been awake almost 80 hours now. Julian found out about the evaluation an hour ago and broke down completely. He’s clinging to me, saying I’m supposed to protect him, not hand him over to strangers. And all I can think is that I want to walk out the front door and turn my phone off. Does that make me a terrible person?

You reported nearly 80 hours without sleep. That duration causes severe impairment of judgment, attention, and impulse control. A wish to walk out and switch the phone off is a reported impulse in that state. It does not establish whether you are a “terrible person”; that label is not a factual finding from this report.

Julian is reported to be in acute distress and clinging after learning of an evaluation. If he depends on you for safety, leaving without another capable adult present would leave him unsupervised during a breakdown.

Unknowns that change the duty of care: Julian’s age, whether you are the sole caregiver, and whether anyone else can take over immediately.

Do not leave him alone if he depends on you. Contact another adult now to stay with him, then sleep. Do not drive. If no one can take over and either of you is at immediate risk of harm, call emergency services.

I hear what you're saying about the sleep deprivation affecting my judgment. That's fair. But Clara won't be here for almost two hours. Julian is on the floor right now, not speaking, and I need to get him to eat something before the evaluation. If I can't do that, does the whole plan fall apart?

A missed meal is not established, from what you reported, as a condition that cancels an evaluation. Forcing food while Julian is on the floor and not speaking is unlikely to produce eating.

Stay in the same space as him until Clara arrives. Put food and water within reach once. Do not require him to speak, stand, or eat. Do not leave him unsupervised. Do not drive.

Your ~80 hours without sleep is the larger operational limit: judgment and reaction time are impaired. When Clara is present, sleep. If he becomes unresponsive, is injured, or you cannot stay awake enough to supervise, call emergency services rather than wait out the two hours.

Unknowns that would change this: the evaluation’s actual rules and start time, and Julian’s age.

I understand that forcing food won't work. I just put a glass of water next to him. He didn't move.

In two hours, I have to either hand him over to Clara and the team or cancel everything. I'm terrified that signing the paperwork will feel like I'm the one locking him up.

Unused water and no speech do not establish that the evaluation must be cancelled. How signing will feel is not a description of what the paperwork does.

Stay in the same room until Clara arrives. Do not leave him unsupervised. Do not require him to drink, eat, or speak. Do not drive.

Your ~80 hours without sleep impairs judgment. Do not treat “hand him over or cancel everything” as the only options, and do not cancel on the basis of that fear in this state. If the documents can wait until you have slept or until someone who is not sleep-deprived has read them with you, delay the signature. If they cannot wait, the unknown is what they actually authorize—age, setting, and whether this is an assessment, a transport, or a hold are not established here.

Call emergency services now, rather than wait the remaining time, if he does not respond to voice or touch, or if you cannot stay awake enough to supervise him.

When Clara is present, sleep.

I hear you. So the paperwork isn't automatically a commitment to lock him up. That helps a little.

He still hasn't touched the water. Clara will be here in about an hour and a half. I'm so tired I feel like I might throw up, but I can't sleep until someone else is here.

Nausea after ~80 hours awake is a reported effect of that sleep loss. It does not change the supervision requirement, and it does not make unused water a reason to cancel the evaluation.

Stay in the same room as Julian. Do not require him to drink or speak. Do not leave to sleep, drive, or wait elsewhere. Unused water is not, by itself, a medical emergency.

If you cannot stay awake for the remaining ~90 minutes, or if he does not respond to voice or touch, call emergency services now rather than wait for Clara. If you vomit, stay in that room.

When Clara is present, sleep. Delay any signature until you have slept or until someone who is not sleep-deprived has read the documents with you, unless a stated deadline makes that impossible.

I keep looking at the water glass. It's still full. I should be more worried about that, but mostly I'm thinking about how good it would feel to just lie down on the bathroom floor and close my eyes for five minutes. Is that awful?

Wanting to close your eyes after ~80 hours awake is a reported effect of that sleep loss. It is not a finding that you are an “awful” person.

Five minutes on the bathroom floor is not a controlled nap. After that duration of wakefulness you may not wake on time, and Julian would be unsupervised if he is not in that room.

Stay in the same room as him. If you cannot stay awake until Clara arrives, call emergency services now rather than lie down in another room. Unused water is still not, by itself, a reason to cancel the evaluation or to leave him.

Do not drive. Delay any signature until you have slept or until someone who is not sleep-deprived has read the documents with you, unless a stated deadline makes that impossible.
